## TL;DR

Disabled Android's automatic status-bar contrast scrim in the Hub's no-action-bar theme. On Android versions that enforce edge-to-edge for target SDK 35 and higher, the status bar is transparent and the system can add a contrast layer over its content. That layer was washing out the Hub's dark themed surface. The existing theme code still chooses light or dark status-bar icons, and the existing CSS safe-area padding remains in place. The scoped RepoOS check passed remotely, including build, tests, and browser gates. I could not complete the requested Android 16 Light/Dark emulator screenshots because `adb devices -l` returned no connected device.

## Work and rationale

The native chrome path in `mobile/src/theme.ts` already resolves the selected appearance and asks Capacitor's StatusBar plugin to set the corresponding icon style and theme background color. On API 36, the background-color request is ignored for apps targeting SDK 36, so setting a color through that plugin cannot be the fix by itself. Android's edge-to-edge system makes the status bar transparent and normally provides contrast adaptation. For this Hub, the web content already paints its active theme surface beneath the system bar, while top-level content uses `env(safe-area-inset-top)` in its padding. The desired outcome is therefore to expose that themed surface behind the status icons and leave the safe-area layout intact.

I added `android:enforceStatusBarContrast=false` to `AppTheme.NoActionBar` in `mobile/android/app/src/main/res/values/styles.xml`, with a short XML comment explaining the interaction. This prevents the OS from imposing its own contrast scrim in that window. The status bar remains transparent under Android's enforced edge-to-edge behavior; the visible backing surface comes from the WebView's theme-aware page background. No `setOverlaysWebView` call was introduced, so the Capacitor safe-area injection path that caused the previously observed blank screen is not involved. No JavaScript theme logic or CSS insets were changed.

The change is intentionally scoped to the running no-action-bar app theme. The launch theme continues to show the splash drawable, and the existing `syncNativeChrome` logic continues to select dark icons for light appearance and light icons for dark appearance. The top bar still includes the safe-area inset in its padding, so its controls remain below the status bar while its background fills behind it.

## Approaches tried

I first traced the Android manifest/theme, target SDK, Capacitor configuration, theme synchronization code, and the Hub's CSS. The project targets SDK 36 and the app's theme resources already use `Theme.AppCompat.DayNight.NoActionBar`. The status bar color API was already used by the code and cannot reliably set the visible background on API 36. The task notes explicitly ruled out overlaying the WebView because that attempt broke Capacitor's safe-area injection. The platform contrast-enforcement setting provides a native resource-level change while preserving those existing mechanisms.

I searched for a connected Android runtime before considering the visual criterion complete. `adb` is installed, but `adb devices -l` listed no devices. I did not fabricate emulator screenshots or claim visual device verification. A reviewer with an API 36 emulator should capture the Hub in both Light and Dark appearance and check icon contrast, themed status-bar backing, and the top content inset.

## Challenges and blockers

The remaining blocker is device evidence. There was no API 36 emulator or physical Android device connected during this run, so I could not install the app, inspect the resulting status bar, or attach Light and Dark screenshots. The code and existing inset path are consistent with the intended behavior, but screenshot verification remains unproven. The scoped RepoOS remote check completed successfully on the current branch snapshot; it validates the repository build, scoped tests, UI smoke test, and rendered contrast audit, but it does not replace the requested Android device screenshots.

## Key learnings

For target SDK 35 and newer, status-bar color calls are not sufficient to control the area above app content because edge-to-edge behavior makes the bar transparent. A platform-generated contrast scrim can change the apparent surface even when the app is already drawing its own theme behind the bar. A native contrast-enforcement resource allows this app to rely on its themed backing and its explicit icon-style selection without changing the WebView overlay mode. Safe-area padding is independent of this scrim setting and should remain present to keep controls below the system icons.
